source: You got some bird seed.
The man covered in snow claims he didn't see anything.
The man covered in snow suspects a woman and her daughter.
The man covered in snow suspects the geezers.
Well, if it isn't the boy who set the neighbourhood right. Come by to do a victory lap, eh? Fine job you did retrieving that part. A fine job indeed.
[Look off into the distance dramatically] All in a day's work.
Thanks man. Happy to help. [Leave]
Aw, it was nothing. Mind if I ask you a few more questions?
...Well, it stands to reason that you would have, well, a reason. In which case, I'd like to know that reason.
You look really dashing right now - like a movie star. I want to capture that.
Look, it's just for a class. No one's going to see it.
(INVESTIGATIVE) Isn't act of photography enough of a reason?
The act? How do you mean, boy? You've piqued my interest.
The reason is born during the act of photography. Its quality is only known after the picture is taken.
Art is expression, and as such, needs no reason. I don't need a reason to smile either, do I?
Isn't there one in the dorm halls? I could have sworn I've seen one.
Oh, that one? Obviously compensating for something.
Oh, that's not a statue. It’s an abomination. Goes against everything that building should stand for.
Hah! Spare me the sarcasm - if anything, it gave rise to some very interesting questions. Some of which I'm hoping to answer today, by hiding the bag of seed, and remaining as motionless as I can.
Motionless? Why?
...And how does that help?

Hah! A somewhat likely scenario, I'll admit. I suppose I was as well, turning their company into a pastime. Either way, that's why I'm attempting a new approach today - hiding my bag of seed and trying to remain motionless.
Motionless? Why?
How does that help?
An interesting hypothesis, and one not too far from my own! That's why I've hidden the bag, you see, and I'm staying as still as is physically possible.
And why exactly are you staying still?

I certainly don't expect to be writing any important papers on it, if that's what you're asking! It's interesting enough in its own right to think about geezers and their perception of the world, don't you think? Sitting here, motionless and observant, is a pleasant enough deviation from my normal routine.
...That's weird.
Normal routine as in...a job?

Oh, I'm an old and stubborn bastard. Experience. Luckily, I'm old enough to have plenty of it by now - but I certainly remember plenty of occasions where I would have done well to take the word of others, too.
You can take my word for it and let me ask you about something else, for starters.
How do you mean?
Sounds pretty smart to me. I'll see you around, old man. [Leave]
Well, you see...Oh. That is a good question. Force of habit, perhaps? I don't suppose you need some birdseed?
I'm good - I'd like to talk more about you, though.
Sure, I'll take some off your hands.
Splendid. Just make sure the geezers don't see you doing it, alright?
Thanks. Now, let's get back to you.
I'll be subtle. Thanks. [Leave]

I suppose I could tell you yes, or even no, but ultimately the thing about experiences is that they need to be...well, experienced. Tell me, do you consider yourself someone who learns through experience, or knowledge?
Experience, I think.
...There's a difference?
Knowledge. Advice. That kind of thing.
Interesting how?
I mean, you look ridiculous.
There's a tragic dignity to your current situation.
Your dashing good looks.
I don't really have time to explain it.

Sometimes, son, you'll be so preoccupied with trying to do the right thing that you inadvertedly end up causing hurt and grief. It is self-centered stubbornness, in the guise of being righteous or kind.
And that's what you did?
...I don't get it.
Many times over, gaining experience each time - experience I hadn't needed, if I had listened.
I see. Mind if I ask you about something else?
Well, thanks for the lecture. See you around. [Leave]

Well, say a friend of yours is hurt by another, over a period of time. You confront them, and the culprit appears remorseful and promises to change. Your hurt friend has reason to believe they won't. Would you forgive the other, and try to help them improve?
Yeah. Everyone deserves a second chance.
No. They've already proven they can't be trusted.

That was my reasoning as well. But the hurt returned - not only did the second friend not change, but I refused to give up even when that, too, added to the hurt of the first. At the end of the day, I lost two friends.
Yeah that...that's not great.
Sounds a little unfair of your first friend, if you ask me.
Everything is clearer in hindsight.
Even more the reason not to engage.
[Walk away in shame]

That willingness to take a side is a sign of someone that learns from knowledge, then. That wasn't my case. I believed I could change someone, and held on to that belief even when proven contrary. Only when I myself was hurt, did I understand - that is the cost of learning by experience.
That's pretty shitty.
So what did you learn, then?
I mean, at least you understand it now.
In some ways, I've grown because of it. In many, I'm sure, I remain the same. We all do bad things, son - what matters is how we deal with them.
...Mind if we talk about something else?
I'm off to deal with some stuff, then. See you. [Leave]
Learning by experience. I hope that clears it all up for you, son.
I think so. Can I ask you about something else?
Yeah. See you around, old man. [Leave]

Every choice you make - or don't make, for that matter - has a million little consequences. I can't control the extent of them, but I can, and should, consider them to the best of my ability. "Learning by experience", make no mistake, is no excuse for being inconsiderate of others or even consequence. That was my lesson.
I think I understand. Mind if we talk about something else now?
For the record, that sounds pretty wise to me. See you around, old man. [Leave]
Lesson's over? Sweet. See you later. [Leave]
No, not necessarily. Shakes things up a bit, I suppose. If I can, I try to avoid staring at the time nowadays.
...Very helpful. Thank you.
Smart.
Any idea who did it?
Certainly - just be subtle about it. Don't want the geezers to notice, you know?
Appreciated. Mind if I ask you about something else?
Thanks. Now let's get back to you.
Great. See you later. [Leave]
Well, whatever it is sounds pretty funny. Shame I'm not in on the joke.
I'm talking about his, you know...his gland. The one between his legs?
You're better off. Let's talk about you some more.
Sorry, it's really nothing. Let's talk about something else.
[Run away, giggling like a madman]
Oh? Well in that case, my boy, perhaps I don't have time to agree either! Thank you for thinking of me, though.
Alright. [Leave]
...Okay, uh. Well. Can I ask you about something else?
All done? Think it will come out alright? I didn't move, did I?
(SARCASTIC) Yeah - truth be told, you're being just a little bit too energetic.
Stellar. Thanks, man.
...I don't know, it's a lot of white. Might end up a little overexposed.
[Shrug] Eh.
Oh. Well, I hope you're right. Of all the things one feels compelled to make up for in lives, something they had no hand in seems like the least shameful...even if that too is misguided.
Right. Let's get back to you, though.
Yeah. Let's talk about something else.
[Run away, giggling like a maniac]

Oh, I only met him briefly at the naming ceremony. Struck me as a terribly worried person. Obsessed with legacy - something of a fool's game, if you ask me. Speaking of which, what do you think of his statue?
I think he's making up for something.
...Statue?
It’s an abomination. Placing it in front of an art school is an affront to everything that building stands for.
Hah! I suppose I do - however, is that really the kind of reputation you want to build as an artist? Not something more serious and dignified?
Nothing's more dignified than making people laugh.
Serious is boring.
Good point. I'll find something a little more poignant. [Leave]
...You alive in there?
...Are you okay, sir?
...Need some help?
Anything else I can help you with?
Yeah, actually there was one thing..
No, I'm off. I've got young kid stuff to do.
Who's to say, boy?
...You?
I mean, you're like covered in snow. And snow is cold.
Like we discussed already, it might have been the geezers. Not sure who else could have done it, so they could be your best bet. Just don't tell them I said so.
Gotcha. Thanks.
I'm afraid not, no. I can keep watch for you from now on, but I doubt I'll be much help. You see, I seem to have come down with a mild case of snowblindness. Hah.
Aw. Thanks anyways.
I'm afraid if I tell you it might undo the work I've put in here today. All I can say is that it's less a matter of 'who' and more a matter of 'what'.
[Whisper] The night goddess.
Yeah, I'm going to need you to spell it out.
...Was it stolen by a stronger, much bigger clock?
Was it the geezers?
From my perspective, I seem to be. But that doesn't necessarily make it so.
Want me to brush some of that snow off you?
...I just want to know if you're okay.
You look cold. Are you cold?
Hah! 'Spurned by Geezers', as it were.
Perfect. You agree to it?
...I'll work on the title later. So you're okay with a picture?
Like I said, the only really suspicious activity I really saw was that mother and her child.
Got it.
Where did they go?
...Well, come to think of it - I did hear this young mother whispering something to her child about the clock. Don't want to make assumptions, but they seemed a little off.
Got it.
Do you know where she went?
They're down the street, eyes fixed on one of the window displays.
Got it
Hello again. Come by to warm me up with some more pleasant conversation?
Something like that. I was hoping to talk to you.
Nah, I'm good. [Leave]
...Possibly, but please don't tell them I told you. I saw them lingering near it, but I can't say for certain.
Understood.
Help? With what?
Dude, you're covered in snow.
Ah yes. Well, that's just a necessary sacrifice I'm willing to make while testing out this little theory of mine.
If you're trying to figure out if snow is cold, I think it's already been proven.
What's the theory?
I'm not entirely sure, I suppose. Depends on how the remainder of the day plays out - but if you're asking if I have any pressing needs, then no. I'm perfectly content.
Want me to brush that snow off you?
You're covered in snow.
Oh, of course not! That would defeat the whole purpose of this little game I'm playing.
What's the name of the game? The talking popsicle?
...So what are you doing, exactly?
I'm trying to determine if it's possible for one to establish a non-transactional relationship with geezers.
Non-transactional?
Geezers?
Hah! No, no - I'm trying to see if it's possible to establish a non-transactional relationship with geezers, you see.
Non-transactional?
Geezers?

Well, you see - every day for the past few years, I've been coming out here to feed the local geezers. I felt like we had established a rapport, a trust. But the other day I forgot to bring my trusty seed bag, and they looked at me like a common stranger. It's then that I realized that maybe I've just been a middle-man to them all along. A bag bearer.
(INVESTIGATIVE) Maybe they think you and the bag are one and the same. Without it, maybe they didn't recognize you.
(SARCASTIC) That must have been so difficult for you. Should I call someone?
(SOCIAL) Maybe they've just assumed you were having a day off. You wouldn't bother your favorite chef for a meal if you met them on the street, would you?
They were using you, man.
Not yet. But that might be due to the cold. I think it might be that they can see my breath. Throws off the statue motif I'm aiming for.
Try holding your breath?
Maybe you should just go back to feeding them.
Maybe you could retry in the summer?
An interesting observation! Maybe, maybe - that's why today I'm trying to establish a new kind of relationship by keeping the bag hidden, and remaining as motionless as possible.
Motionless? Why?
How does that help?
I actually don't know. Could you spell it out for me?
[Giggle uncontrollably]
His, um...height.
His, um...penis...
You know. I'm talking about his...[point to crotch]
Sorry, I'm being silly. Let's talk more about you.
Alright - I might have seen the G-E-E-Z-E-R-S poking around near the clock. Could be because I haven't been feeding them today, and they got desperate for a snack.
Thanks. I'll try to leave your name out of it.

If it was, I'm very sorry to say that I must have missed out on that spectacle. If anything, I think the geezers have been a little restless lately. I think it might be because I haven't been feeding them today. Might have got desperate and snagged a hand instead.
Thanks. I'll try to keep you out of it.
Hah! You might be right about that. Alright then. Shoot away!
[Take picture]

Well, I've seen plenty of geezers establish bonds with inanimate objects when there's nothing for them to gain. Statues, bike racks, fire hydrants. So I'm trying to discover if it's possible to develop a similar bond.
What are you hoping to get out of that, exactly?
That's nuts.
Sounds like you need a job.
Heh. Perhaps it is! But it occupies the time, same as our conversation is now. How come the curiosity? Let me guess: a student?
How did you know that?
Nailed it.
Happily retired, thank you very much - and I'd wager you, since we're on the topic, don't even have a job to retire from! Let me guess, you're a student?
Yep.
...How'd you know that?

I've seen plenty of geezers establish bonds with inanimate objects when there's nothing for them to gain. Statues, bike racks, fire hydrants, et cetera. I'm trying to discover if it's possible to develop a similar bond.
What are you hoping to get out of that, exactly?
That's nuts.
Maybe you should just get a job.
Your voice. Youthful, yet to be marred by the realities of life. I'm guessing you're here for the purposes of an assignment - either creative writing or...photography?
...Are you a psychic?
Photography.
And you're here for an assignment, I'm guessing? Either photography or, hmm...some sort of creative writing.
...Are you psychic or something?
Yeah, I'm a photography major.

Hah! No, just an old teacher who knows it's finally project season and the particular qualities of Gastown tend to attract students looking to take advantage of its extremes. So, was I right? What kind of student are you?
I'm a photography student.
Alright, then, what can I do for you?
Mind if I take a picture of you?
That's all. Goodbye.
I'd like to know a bit more about you.
Any idea what happened to that clock?

Ah, a "Thaddeus Rock-er"! I taught a few buildings down from yours, you see - 'The Chauncey Billingsly Department of Physics'. I'm guessing Chauncey was an odd one himself, but he was long before even my time. I digress, though. Is there something you need?
I was wondering if I could ask you some questions?
Nothing. Just wondering about the snow. [Leave]
You're the artist! I'm just the tragically dignified subject. Shoot away.
[Take picture]
Stand for? What does a “building” stand for, besides keeping out wind and rain?
Art.
Higher learning.
Good point. Let's talk more about you.
It's not my field, but shouldn't great art stand for itself?
I'm not looking to make great art. I'm looking to make money.
Yeah, but what about the bad art? Like the statue?
No.
Shoot away, my boy!
[Take picture]
And what might that be?
His wicked ways.
Having a small...you know.
A misspent life.
Hmm. Well, he wouldn't be the first. At least he's trying to make up for them. So many don't.
Let's get back to you, though.
Let's talk about something else.
Good point. I'm going to bounce. [Leave]
Well, to be blunt, if all it takes to interfere with your studies is a garish statue, I'm not sure the obstacle is the root of the problem.
Nuh-uh. The statue is my only problem.
Okay, let's get back to you.
I'd assume there'd be no harm in letting it fall.
Interesting. I'd like to know more about you, though.
Hmm. Let's talk about something else.
Great. Good talk. [Leave]
Now, now, my boy. I wasn't born yesterday. I know how silly I look at the present moment  - why don't you just say that?
Okay. You look silly. Foolish, even.
I don't like confrontations ... [Leaves awkwardly]
I do. But it's sealed tight so as not to interfere with my little geezer gambit.
Makes sense. Got another question for you.
Mind if I take some?
(INVESTIGATIVE) If you weren't intent on feeding them today, why did you even bring it?
Hmm. Fascinating.
I have some more questions about you.
You know what fascinates me? You. Let's talk more about that.
Let's talk about something else.
I'm going to go. [Leave]
Perhaps you should take up sculpture then. I happen to know that statue cost a fortune.
Maybe I will. Let's get back to you, though.
[Let's talk about something else]
Good advice. [Leave]
Because you have no real choice in the matter. And no way of knowing whether you've succeeded.
I don't know. Wouldn't you like to have a statue of yourself someday?
Getting a statue of yourself seems like a good start.
I just want to be remembered after I'm gone.
...No, no. I mean the geezers. Just don't tell them I said so. Don't want to sabotage my little experiment, don't you know?
Oh, that does make more sense.

Like Thaddeus? But neither of us knows a thing about him except what he looks like gilded in bronze. And how long will that last? The minute that building becomes obsolete they’ll melt him down and use it to edify the next soul that picks up the tab. That’s hardly legacy. It’s just extending the half-life of your name.
If you say so, man. [Leave]
Mind if we extend this conversation in a different direction?

But isn't that just extending the half-life of your obscelence? All names are forgotten eventually. How many names do you know from before the creation of the Wall? It all feels more like a contest to see whose death has the biggest echo.
Well, my name's Howard. I'll see you around. [Leave]
I think I get what you're saying. Listen, can I ask you about something else?
Not really. Though I might if the dedication ceremony had an after party. Thaddeus's had an open bar. I like an open bar.
Me too. Let's talk a bit more about you.
Same. I might go looking for one right now. [Leave]

I’d like to think it would have been through my work: maybe some student I inspired, a theorem I helped solve. But that’s vanity. The universe is so vast and interconnected that my greatest impact more likely will be something far more inconsequential. Throwing a stone into the ocean as a child, perhaps.
How would throwing a stone be your legacy?
(SARCASTIC) That'd have to be one big stone.
Shall I explain? Or do you just want to make fun?
Sorry. Please explain.
I want to make fun.

Suppose I hadn't moved that stone. It stays on the shore for generations. One day a genious, in deep thought, trips on it right as they're about to have a breakthrough solution to a problem that affects us all. They're never able to reach it again, and subsequently, the problem remains a problem - all due to that stone.
What an asshole. The stone, I mean.
Okay, I follow...
...You're losing me.
A picture of me? Why?
Why not?
(SOCIAL) I'm need an interesting image for my final project, and you sir, definitely qualify.
Nevermind, actually.
That's fine. We should talk about something lighter then. Your choice.
Let's talk more about you.
No. I'm sorry, that was rude. Explain how throwing a stone in an ocean could be your legacy.

Or maybe it's the reverse: maybe the stone was poised to interrupt the stroll of some would-be fascist tyrant, who—now free to stroll the beach without interruption—will have the extended calm and clarity of mind to begin questioning his ideology, sparing us all from a grim future. The consequences of small actions cannot be underestimated.
Time for me to go throw some stones. [Leave]
That sounds pretty far-fetched.
That's kind of depressing.
I like that theory.

Absolutely. But of all the seemingly infinitesimal changes our existence will inflict upon this world, it seems equally far-fetched for our most impactful moment to also be the one that makes us the most proud. Or the most ashamed.
Cool. Let's get back to you, though.
Yeah...let's talk about something else. Anything else, really.
(SOCIAL) I think my most impactful gesture will be the picture I’m about to take of you.
Hah! Fair enough.
Anyway, I'm off. Later, snow man. [Leave]
Mind if I ask you about something else?
Could be - or is it an invitation to stop overthinking one's choices? And instead simply...'be'.
Sounds more like giving up.
[Just be]
Then far be it from me to stop you from fulfilling your destiny.
[Take picture]
I'm sensing by the furrow in your brow that you're actively trying to 'be'. Which is the opposite of what I'm proposing.
Sorry. Um, let's talk about something else. Anything else, really.
[Just be, but harder this time]
Well, if that's your take away don't try it until you've retired. Earning a living is still fairly important. If only for the comfort it brings.
Sorry. Um, let's talk about something else. Anything else, really.
Hmm. Maybe you're just constipated.
Um...let's talk about you some more.
...Can we change the subject?
[Leave]
As do I. It takes the stress off overthinking one's actions and allows you to just...'be'.
Let's keep talking about you.
Let's talk about something else.
[Leave]
[Just be]
Oh? Well, then - ask away.
Any luck with the geezers yet?
Did you know Thaddeus Rock?
Why is worrying about legacy a fool's game?
What do you think your legacy will be?
Do you still have some of that birdseed?
Are you sure you don't want me to brush some of that snow off you?
Never truly know something until you see it yourself, eh? Not necessarily a bad quality, not at all. Lends itself well to confidence, which a similarly double-edged sword.
Great talk. Can we redirect it to another topic?
How about yourself?
...Well, I'm off to go experience more stuff, then. Later. [Leave]
Ah! If you'll allow me to make an assumption, then, I'd wager experience in your case.
Great talk. Can we redirect it to another topic?
How about yourself?
...Well, I'm off to go experience something else, then. Later. [Leave]
Hmmm...it may have to come to that. But I'll give them a few more hours. It might just be that they're shy.
Mind if I ask you some more questions?
Suit yourself, man. [Leave]
At my age? Shepherd no, I'd drop dead within a minute! Hah!
Mind if I ask you some more questions?
Well, we tried. [Leave]
A fine quality to have - not necessarily better than the other, but a fine quality nonetheless. We should all strive to listen more.
Great talk. Can we redirect it to another topic?
How about yourself?
Sure. I'll go listen to some other people, then. See ya. [Leave]
Now, now. Don't be ridiculous. I don't much appreciate having my leg pulled like that.
Pulling legs? You look cool as fuck, bro. I'm serious.
[Flirt] I'd be happy to pull something besides your leg...
Fine. You look silly as fuck and I think that'll make people smile.
But in that case, why even take it? Surely, it must have a purpose other than obligation.
You look really handsome right now. Hot, even.
I guess it would be funny. You look ridiculous, man. Might crack people up.
...Not really, no.
Hah! Never thought of it like that before - I suppose that's why I never lectured in the arts, eh? Very interesting, my boy, and I won't argue. Shoot away!
[Take picture]
Oh. Well, apology accepted. No hard feelings whatsoever - but now, will you tell me why you want a picture of me?
...I think there's a certain sense of tranquility to you. I want to try to capture it and share it with others.
It might make people laugh. You look kind of funny.
Now there's a noble goal, and steeped in honesty to boot! Was that so hard?
Not really.
Kind of. Yeah.
Oh, yes, it's missing a hand, isn't it?
...Any strong feelings about that?
Any idea who did it?
Well, perhaps that's what makes it worth doing! Now go on - take your silly picture and bring some levity to your class.
[Take picture]
And now you know that for next time. Go ahead and take your picture, boy.
[Take picture]

...Well. In that case, I hope you'll understand that I respectfully decline. I'm all for engaging students, but only as long as they have genuine interest. Maybe you'll find some other subject that intrigues you.
Thanks, anyway. [leave]

Hmm. Well, as much as I would like to help a wayward student with their final project, I think the best lesson I can give you right now is to refuse you what you want. I suggest you take that with you and reflect on it before you approach someone else like...that.
But...I was being serious.
(SOCIAL) Wait, hold on. I misread the situation, and tried making a joke. I'm sorry.
...Understood. Sorry. [Leave]

You're very kind to offer, but I'm quite alright. I'm cold, but at the same time, the snow is rather insulating. Keeps me warm. Of course, part of me is still fighting the temptation to brush it off. Really makes you cognisant of the moment.
The moment looks uncomfortable.
...And why is that a good thing?
You're saying it's a...valuable experience?

Hah! It feels that way too - but I suppose that's the whole point, isn't it? I'm plenty comfortable most of the time, so I'm sure I can live without it for a few hours. Experience broadens the mind, and all that.
I guess so. Can I ask you about something else?
You do you, man. [Leave]
What do you mean by that?
I'm not entirely sure, dear boy. It's interesting, and at my age, interesting is appealing. Do you see what I mean?
Can't say that I do.
...I think so, actually.
I think I want to know more.
Hm. Perhaps one day, you will. Until then, you'll just have to bear the confusion!
Let's talk a bit more about you.
Let's talk about something else.
Stay warm, man. [Leave]
Well, then - maybe one day you'll be sitting motionless on a bench on a park as well, reflecting on life! Hah!
Let's talk about something else.
